links.outcome: AI cephalometric measurement agreement under incorrect head positioning versus correct positioning
links.effect: Positional errors drastically reduced measurement accuracy; linear parameters such as Go-Me showed poorest agreement across all software; WebCeph and Ceph Assistant linear ICC < 0.50.
links.quote: Positional errors drastically reduced measurement accuracy, with linear parameters such as Go-Me showing the poorest agreement across all software.

links.outcome: AI software accuracy variation across three products and measurement types
links.effect: AudaxCeph achieved excellent agreement (ICC > 0.90) for several skeletal parameters but failed on soft tissue; WebCeph and Ceph Assistant showed greater variability (ICC < 0.50 for linear measures).
links.quote: AudaxCeph demonstrated the most consistent accuracy, achieving excellent agreement (ICC > 0.90) for several skeletal parameters; however, it failed in detecting soft tissue accurately.

screen.reason: Evaluates the robustness of three commercial automated AI cephalometric software programs on images with correct vs incorrect head positions compared to manual reference tracing.
